title: US tariffs pass through to consumer prices directly and later through domestic inputs and markups
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35561, The Anatomy of Tariff Pass-through into Consumer Prices
geography: United States; goods exposed to the 2025-2026 US tariffs

observations.period: 2025-2026 US tariffs; consumer-price pass-through relative to less-exposed goods

denominator.unit: tariff-exposed goods and comparison goods; abstract does not disclose the full product, firm, or transaction count

total_pass_through.unit: percent of the tariff increase passed through to consumer prices

comparison.value: Estimate is measured relative to less-exposed goods while holding aggregate conditions fixed

domestic_price_scope.value: Tariffs raise prices of goods made at home as well as the imports directly taxed

observations.method: Empirical analysis of 2025-2026 US tariff exposure and consumer prices, comparing more- and less-exposed goods while holding aggregate conditions fixed.
observations.uncertainty: The abstract does not disclose the complete product universe, sample counts, confidence intervals, or all controls; the estimate is relative to less-exposed goods and is not a universal price effect for every household or product.
observations.subgroup: Consumers purchasing tariff-exposed goods, domestic producers using imported inputs, foreign varieties, and less-exposed comparison goods.
observations.counterinterpretation: Observed price changes can also reflect demand, exchange rates, inventories, retail margins, product substitution, or macroeconomic conditions not captured by the bounded abstract result.

observations.period: 2025-2026 US tariffs; decomposition of consumer-price pass-through

denominator.unit: percent of the estimated tariff-to-consumer-price increase

direct_component.unit: percent of the estimated consumer-price increase attributable to higher prices of foreign varieties

indirect_component.unit: percent of the estimated consumer-price increase attributable to imported-input costs and domestic markup increases

market_power_channel.value: Domestic producers raise markups when higher-priced imports reduce competition

observations.method: Decomposition of the total estimated consumer-price pass-through into direct import-price and indirect domestic-input/markup channels.
observations.uncertainty: The decomposition is conditional on the paper's model and empirical design; it does not establish that every domestic producer gains market power or that markups rise in every sector.
observations.subgroup: Foreign varieties, US producers using imported inputs, domestic competitors, retailers, and consumers with different product substitutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Domestic markup movement may reflect cost recovery, demand shifts, inventory dynamics, or strategic repositioning rather than pure exploitation of reduced import competition.

observations.period: 2025-2026 US tariffs; timing of supply-chain transmission

denominator.unit: tariff-exposed supply chains; abstract reports a timing pattern rather than a disclosed count

direct_timing.value: Direct pass-through occurs quickly because tariffs raise import prices almost immediately

indirect_timing.value: Indirect pass-through through imported inputs and domestic pricing takes nine to twelve months

household_implication.value: Consumer-price effects are larger and more drawn out than a direct-import-only estimate would imply

observations.method: Dynamic comparison of direct import-price transmission and delayed supply-chain/input-cost transmission.
observations.uncertainty: The lag is an estimated aggregate timing pattern; it does not identify which households experience the largest burden, how retailers adjust, or whether consumers switch products or suppliers.
observations.subgroup: Households with different budgets and product baskets, domestic producers with different imported-input exposure, and retailers facing different inventory cycles.
observations.counterinterpretation: Inventory, contracts, hedging, exchange rates, or delayed demand changes could alter the timing for particular products and firms.

related_sources.claim: Official NBER landing page with the 2025-2026 tariff exposure, 26 percent pass-through estimate, direct/indirect decomposition, and nine-to-twelve-month lag.
NBER DOI route for the working paper.

boundary: This record adds a US consumer-price and firm-market-power mechanism: tariffs can pass through directly to imported varieties and indirectly through domestic input costs and markups over a longer supply-chain lag. It does not establish household welfare, incidence by income, retailer behavior, firm profitability, substitution, employment, or a universal tariff effect outside the study design.
